subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The Weimar Republic was established in Germany in:
questions.explain: Germany became a democratic republic after WWI, with a new constitution in 1919.

questions.q: The Treaty of Versailles caused resentment in Germany because it:
options: Imposed reparations, territorial losses and a 'war guilt' clause
questions.explain: Many Germans saw the treaty as a humiliating 'diktat'.
The 1923 crisis destroyed savings as money became almost worthless.

questions.q: Under Gustav Stresemann in the mid-1920s, Germany:
options: Recovered economically, helped by the Dawes Plan
questions.explain: US loans (Dawes Plan) and new currency stabilised Weimar Germany.

questions.q: Hitler's failed attempt to seize power in Munich in 1923 was the:
questions.explain: The Beer Hall (Munich) Putsch failed and Hitler was imprisoned, writing Mein Kampf.

questions.q: The Great Depression from 1929 helped the Nazis because it caused:
options: Mass unemployment and desperation, increasing support for extreme parties
questions.explain: Economic collapse boosted support for the Nazis and Communists.

questions.q: Hitler was appointed Chancellor of Germany in:
questions.explain: Hitler became Chancellor in 1933, then rapidly established a dictatorship.

questions.q: The Reichstag Fire (1933) was used by the Nazis to:
options: Pass emergency laws and suppress the Communists
questions.explain: The fire justified the Reichstag Fire Decree, curbing civil liberties.

questions.q: The 1933 law that allowed Hitler to make laws without the Reichstag was the:
questions.explain: The Enabling Act gave Hitler dictatorial powers.

questions.q: The Nazi secret police were the:
questions.explain: The Gestapo and SS enforced conformity through fear and terror.

questions.q: The Night of the Long Knives (1934) saw Hitler:
options: Eliminate rivals, including the SA leadership
questions.explain: Hitler purged the SA leadership (Rohm) to secure army support and his own power.

questions.q: The Nazi youth organisation for boys was the:
questions.explain: Nazi youth groups indoctrinated young people with Nazi ideology.

questions.q: The 1935 laws removing Jewish rights and citizenship were the:
questions.explain: The Nuremberg Laws stripped Jews of citizenship and banned marriage with non-Jews.

questions.q: The organised attack on Jewish homes, shops and synagogues in 1938 was:
questions.explain: Kristallnacht ('Night of Broken Glass') marked a violent escalation of persecution.

questions.q: Nazi propaganda, led by Goebbels, aimed to:
options: Control opinion and build support for Hitler and Nazi ideas
questions.explain: Propaganda and censorship shaped public opinion in the dictatorship.

questions.q: The Nazis maintained control through a combination of:
options: Propaganda (persuasion) and terror (the SS and Gestapo)
Free elections and a free press
questions.explain: Persuasion plus fear allowed the Nazis to consolidate a totalitarian state.

specSource: Eduqas GCSE History specification; Non-British study in depth: Germany in Transition
